questions.q: Which business process does Oracle Fusion Receivables sit inside?
options: Order-to-Cash
Procure-to-Pay
Hire-to-Retire
Plan-to-Produce
questions.explain: Receivables owns the invoicing and collection steps of Order-to-Cash: billing the customer and collecting what they owe.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable?
options: They are unrelated modules with no shared concepts
Payables tracks what a business owes; Receivables tracks what a business is owed, as a mirror process
Receivables is a report that summarizes Payables data
Payables only exists in Oracle EBS, not Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Payables is Procure-to-Pay (money going out); Receivables is Order-to-Cash (money coming in). Both are subledgers feeding General Ledger.

questions.q: Which two paths can bring a transaction into Receivables?
options: Only manual entry; Receivables cannot import data
Email and fax only
Manual entry and AutoInvoice import
Only AutoInvoice; manual entry was removed in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Transactions are either keyed directly into the Transactions Workbench, or imported and validated through AutoInvoice from an upstream source system.

questions.q: In the Northwind Fixtures Co. example, what happens in the accounting when the invoice is first created?
options: Cash is debited and Revenue is credited
Accounts Receivable is credited and Cash is debited
No accounting entry is created until the customer pays
Accounts Receivable is debited and Revenue is credited
questions.explain: Billing creates a receivable: debit Accounts Receivable, credit Revenue. The debit to Cash only happens later, when the receipt is applied.

questions.q: Besides General Ledger, which other two areas does Receivables data flow into downstream?
options: Cash Management and Collections
Fixed Assets and Procurement
Payroll and Benefits
Inventory and Order Management only
questions.explain: Receipt data flows to Cash Management for bank reconciliation, and open overdue balances drive Collections and dunning activity.
